name: Dameng (DM)
tagline: China's leading home-grown RDBMS; DM9 (2026) adds distributed, HTAP and AI features.
description: Dameng's DM database is a fully self-developed relational database from Wuhan Dameng Database Co., which listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2024. Unlike several Chinese competitors it is not a PostgreSQL fork, yet it offers strong Oracle compatibility (PL/SQL-like DMSQL, similar system views), a shared-storage cluster (DMDSC), MPP for analytics and data-guard style replication. DM8 has been the workhorse in government, power-grid and finance migrations; DM9, released in April 2026 after a seven-year gap, adds a unified centralized/distributed architecture, HTAP and AI capabilities. Like its peers, it is almost entirely focused on the Chinese market.

pricing.notes: Commercial editions; a free development edition of DM8 is downloadable.

scale.notes: DMDSC shared-storage clustering, MPP for analytics and a distributed architecture in DM9.

strengths: Independently developed kernel, not a fork, which matters for Chinese procurement rules
Strong Oracle compatibility in SQL, PL/SQL and system catalogues
Shared-storage cluster (DMDSC) and MPP options cover OLTP HA and analytics
Large installed base in government, power and finance migrations
weaknesses: Ecosystem, docs and support are almost entirely Chinese
DM9 is new; most production references are still on DM8
Vendor performance claims are rarely independently benchmarked
useCases: Replacing Oracle in government and state-owned enterprises
Financial back-office systems on domestic infrastructure
